label: UniFi Industrial DIN 8
description: UniFi Industrial DIN 8 (USW-Industrial-DIN-8) - 8x 1G RJ45 + 2x 1G SFP. 20 Gbps switching capacity.
notes: PoE, read 2026-11-28. `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/usw-industrial-din-8` (HTTP 200, 640,296 B, server-rendered table) prints **Port Layout: 1 GbE RJ45 8 (1G/100M/10M), 1G SFP 2, Console 1**, **Redundancy: (2) DC inputs**, **Max. Power Consumption 12W**, **Power Method: (2) 2-pin DC inputs with terminal block**, **Power Input Method: DC input** and **Supported Voltage Range 12-60V DC**. The Hardware block has no PoE row and the Overview has no PoE section. The vendor does print one when the hardware has it: the sibling row `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/usw-industrial-din-8-poe` (HTTP 200, 646,721 B) carries **Port Layout 8 (All PoE++)**, **PoE Ports: PoE++**, **Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE: PoE++**, **Max. PoE Output: Up to PoE++**, **Total PoE Availability** and **Max. Power Consumption 12W (Excluding PoE Output) / 492W (Including PoE Output)** - a different SKU with its own budget. So the plain DIN 8's silence is a product decision, not a blank field: its 8 copper ports carry `poeIn: false`. Without it `isPoePd()` matched `unifi` in the label ("UniFi Industrial DIN 8") and inferred 12.95 W on each - **103.6 W** drawn from a PSE by an industrial switch fed from a 12-60V DC terminal block whose total draw is 12 W.
